## Summary

This pull request is created by [StepSecurity](https://app.stepsecurity.io/securerepo) at the request of @Raj-StepSecurity. Please merge the Pull Request to incorporate the requested changes. Please tag @Raj-StepSecurity on your message if you have any questions related to the PR.
## Security Fixes

### Pinned Dependencies

GitHub Action tags and Docker tags are mutable. This poses a security risk. GitHub's Security Hardening guide recommends pinning actions to full length commit.

- [GitHub Security Guide](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions#using-third-party-actions)
- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#pinned-dependencies)
### Keeping your actions up to date with Dependabot

With Dependabot version updates, when Dependabot identifies an outdated dependency, it raises a pull request to update the manifest to the latest version of the dependency. This is recommended by GitHub as well as The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF).

- [GitHub Security Guide](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/dependabot/working-with-dependabot/keeping-your-actions-up-to-date-with-dependabot)
- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#dependency-update-tool)
### Detect Vulnerabilities with SAST Workflow 

Static Code Analysis (also known as Source Code Analysis) is usually performed as part of a Code Review (also known as clear-box testing) and is carried out at the Implementation phase of a Security Development Lifecycle (SDL). Static Code Analysis commonly refers to the running of Static Code Analysis tools that attempt to highlight possible vulnerabilities within ‘static’ (non-running) source code by using techniques such as Taint Analysis and Data Flow Analysis.

- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://github.c

GitHub Action tags and Docker tags are mutable. This poses a security risk. GitHub's Security Hardening guide recommends pinning actions to full length commit.

- [GitHub Security Guide](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions#using-third-party-actions)

- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#dependency-update-tool)

Static Code Analysis (also known as Source Code Analysis) is usually performed as part of a Code Review (also known as clear-box testing) and is carried out at the Implementation phase of a Security Development Lifecycle (SDL). Static Code Analysis commonly refers to the running of Static Code Analysis tools that attempt to highlight possible vulnerabilities within ‘static’ (non-running) source code by using techniques such as Taint Analysis and Data Flow Analysis.

- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://gi

- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#pinned-dependencies)

The action scans for vulnerable versions of dependencies introduced by package version changes in pull requests, and warns you about the associated security vulnerabilities. This gives you better visibility of what's changing in a pull request, and helps prevent vulnerabilities being added to your repository.

## Security Fixes

### Pinned Dependencies

GitHub Action tags and Docker tags are mutable. This poses a security risk. GitHub's Security Hardening guide recommends pinning actions to full length commit.

- [GitHub Security Guide](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions#using-third-party-actions)

### Replaced with StepSecurity Maintained Actions

Some third-party GitHub Actions used in this repository are unmaintained (archived, or with no updates in over a year). They have been replaced with their StepSecurity Maintained equivalents, which are actively maintained and kept up to date.

An action is replaced only when the StepSecurity Maintained equivalent publishes a matching major version tag, and the replacement keeps that same major version (for example, `some-org/some-action@v1` → `step-security/some-action@v1`). Actions whose maintained equivalent has no matching major version are left unchanged.

- [StepSecurity Maintained Actions](https://docs.stepsecurity.io/github-actions/actions/stepsecurity-maintained-actions)

## Security Fixes

### Detect Vulnerabilities with SAST Workflow 

Static Code Analysis (also known as Source Code Analysis) is usually performed as part of a Code Review (also known as clear-box testing) and is carried out at the Implementation phase of a Security Development Lifecycle (SDL). Static Code Analysis commonly refers to the running of Static Code Analysis tools that attempt to highlight possible vulnerabilities within ‘static’ (non-running) source code by using techniques such as Taint Analysis and Data Flow Analysis.

- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#sast)
- [OWASP Static Code Analysis](https://owasp.org/www-community/controls/Static_Code_Analysis)

### Maintain Code Quality with Pre-Commit

Pre-commit is a framework for managing and maintaining multi-language pre-commit hooks. Hooks can be any scripts, code, or binaries that run at any stage of the git workflow. Pre-commit hooks are useful for enforcing code quality, code formatting, and detecting security vulnerabilities.

- [Official Pre-commit documentation](https://pre-commit.com/)
- [Getting Started guide](https://pre-commit.com/#getting-started)

## Security Fixes

### Keeping your actions up to date with Dependabot

With Dependabot version updates, when Dependabot identifies an outdated dependency, it raises a pull request to update the manifest to the latest version of the dependency. This is recommended by GitHub as well as The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF).

- [GitHub Security Guide](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/dependabot/working-with-dependabot/keeping-your-actions-up-to-date-with-dependabot)
- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#dependency-update-tool)
### Secure Dockerfiles

Pin image tags to digests in Dockerfiles. With the Docker v2 API release, it became possible to use digests in place of tags when pulling images or to use them in FROM lines in Dockerfiles.

- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#pinned-dependencies)
### Add Dependency Review Workflow

The Dependency Review Workflow enforces dependency reviews on your pull requests. The action scans for vulnerable versions of dependencies introduced by package version changes in pull requests, and warns you about the associated security vulnerabilities. This gives you better visibility of what's changing in a pull request, and helps prevent vulnerabilities being added to your repository.

- [Github Guide about Dependency Review](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/supply-chain-security/understanding-your-software-supply-chain/about-dependency-review)
- [Github Guide for Configuring Dependency Review Action](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/supply-chain-security/understand

## Security Fixes

### Keeping your actions up to date with Dependabot

With Dependabot version updates, when Dependabot identifies an outdated dependency, it raises a pull request to update the manifest to the latest version of the dependency. This is recommended by GitHub as well as The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF).

- [GitHub Security Guide](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/dependabot/working-with-dependabot/keeping-your-actions-up-to-date-with-dependabot)
- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#dependency-update-tool)
### Add Dependency Review Workflow

The Dependency Review Workflow enforces dependency reviews on your pull requests. The action scans for vulnerable versions of dependencies introduced by package version changes in pull requests, and warns you about the associated security vulnerabilities. This gives you better visibility of what's changing in a pull request, and helps prevent vulnerabilities being added to your repository.

- [Github Guide about Dependency Review](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/supply-chain-security/understanding-your-software-supply-chain/about-dependency-review)
- [Github Guide for Configuring Dependency Review Action](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/supply-chain-security/understanding-your-software-supply-chain/configuring-dependency-review#using-inline-configuration-to-set-up-the-dependency-review-action)
### Add OpenSSF Scorecard Workflow

OpenSSF Scorecard is an automated tool that assesses a number of important heuristics ("checks") associated with software security and assigns each check a score of 0-10. Y

### Pinned Dependencies

A *pinned dependency* is a dependency that is explicitly set to a specific hashed version instead of a mutable version. Pinned dependencis ensure that development and deployment are done with the same software versions which reduces deployment risks, and enables reproducibility. Please tag @guidezpl on your message if you have any questions related to the PR. You can also engage with the [StepSecurity](https://github.com/step-security) team by tagging @step-security-bot.

## Security Fixes

### Pinned Dependencies

A *pinned dependency* is a dependency that is explicitly set to a specific hashed version instead of a mutable version. Pinned dependencis ensure that development and deployment are done with the same software versions which reduces deployment risks, and enables reproducibility. It can help mitigate compromised dependencies from undermining the security of the project in certain scenarios. The dependencies were pinned using [Secure WorkFlows](https://github.com/step-security/secure-workflows)

- [GitHub Security Guide](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions#using-third-party-actions)

## Security Fixes

Static Code Analysis (also known as Source Code Analysis) is usually performed as part of a Code Review (also known as clear-box testing) and is carried out at the Implementation phase of a Security Development Lifecycle (SDL). Static Code Analysis commonly refers to the running of Static Code Analysis tools that attempt to highlight possible vulnerabilities within ‘static’ (non-running) source code by using techniques such as Taint Analysis and Data Flow Analysis.

## Security Fixes

### Add Dependency Review Workflow

The Dependency Review Workflow enforces dependency reviews on your pull requests. The action scans for vulnerable versions of dependencies introduced by package version changes in pull requests, and warns you about the associated security vulnerabilities. This gives you better visibility of what's changing in a pull request, and helps prevent vulnerabilities being added to your repository.

## Summary

This pull request has been generated by [StepSecurity](https://app.stepsecurity.io/github/step-security/actions/dashboard) as part of your enterprise subscription to ensure compliance with recommended security best practices. Please review and merge the pull request to apply these security enhancements.

## Security Fixes

### Harden Runner

Harden-Runner is an open-source security agent for the GitHub-hosted runner to prevent software supply chain attacks. It prevents exfiltration of credentials, detects tampering of source code during build, and enables running jobs without sudo access.

- [GitHub Security Guide](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions)
- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#dangerous-workflow)
### Least Privileged GitHub Actions Token Permissions

The GITHUB_TOKEN is an automatically generated secret to make authenticated calls to the GitHub API. GitHub recommends setting minimum token permissions for the GITHUB_TOKEN.

- [GitHub Security Guide](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-guides/automatic-token-authentication#using-the-github_token-in-a-workflow)
- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#token-permissions)

### Pinned Dependencies

Pinning GitHub Actions to specific versions or commit SHAs ensures that your workflows remain consistent and secure.
Unpinned actions can lead to unexpected changes or vulnerabilities caused by upstream updates.

- [GitHub Security Guide](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions#using-third-party-actions)

## Security Fixes

### Add Dependency Review Workflow

The Dependency Review Workflow enforces dependency reviews on your pull requests. The action scans for vulnerable versions of dependencies introduced by package version changes in pull requests, and warns you about the associated security vulnerabilities. This gives you better visibility of what's changing in a pull request, and helps prevent vulnerabilities being added to your repository.

## Security Fixes

### Add OpenSSF Scorecard Workflow

OpenSSF Scorecard is an automated tool that assesses a number of important heuristics ("checks") associated with software security and assigns each check a score of 0-10. You can use these scores to understand specific areas to improve in order to strengthen the security posture of your project.

Scorecard workflow also allows maintainers to display a Scorecard badge on their repository to show off their hard work.

- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Scorecard](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard)
### Maintain Code Quality with Pre-Commit

Pre-commit is a framework for managing and maintaining multi-language pre-commit hooks. Hooks can be any scripts, code, or binaries that run at any stage of the git workflow. Pre-commit hooks are useful for enforcing code quality, code formatting, and detecting security vulnerabilities.

- [Official Pre-commit documentation](https://pre-commit.com/)
- [Getting Started guide](https://pre-commit.com/#getting-started)

## Summary

This pull request has been generated by [StepSecurity](https://app.stepsecurity.io/github/step-security/actions/dashboard) as part of your enterprise subscription to ensure compliance with recommended security best practices. Please review and merge the pull request to apply these security enhancements.

## Security Fixes

### Harden Runner

Harden-Runner is an open-source security agent for the GitHub-hosted runner to prevent software supply chain attacks. It prevents exfiltration of credentials, detects tampering of source code during build, and enables running jobs without sudo access.

- [GitHub Security Guide](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions)
- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#dangerous-workflow)
### Least Privileged GitHub Actions Token Permissions

The GITHUB_TOKEN is an automatically generated secret to make authenticated calls to the GitHub API. GitHub recommends setting minimum token permissions for the GITHUB_TOKEN.

- [GitHub Security Guide](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-guides/automatic-token-authentication#using-the-github_token-in-a-workflow)
- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#token-permissions)

### Pinned Dependencies

Pinning GitHub Actions to specific versions or commit SHAs ensures that your workflows remain consistent and secure.
Unpinned actions can lead to unexpected changes or vulnerabilities caused by upstream updates.

- [GitHub Security Guide](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions#using-third-party-actions)
- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#pinned-dependencies)

## Summary

This pull request is created by [StepSecurity](https://app.stepsecurity.io/securerepo) at the request of @4alvit. Please merge the Pull Request to incorporate the requested changes. Please tag @4alvit on your message if you have any questions related to the PR.
## Security Fixes

### Keeping your actions up to date with Dependabot

With Dependabot version updates, when Dependabot identifies an outdated dependency, it raises a pull request to update the manifest to the latest version of the dependency. This is recommended by GitHub as well as The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF).

- [GitHub Security Guide](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/dependabot/working-with-dependabot/keeping-your-actions-up-to-date-with-dependabot)
- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#dependency-update-tool)
### Secure Dockerfiles

Pin image tags to digests in Dockerfiles. With the Docker v2 API release, it became possible to use digests in place of tags when pulling images or to use them in FROM lines in Dockerfiles.

- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#pinned-dependencies)
### Add Dependency Review Workflow

The Dependency Review Workflow enforces dependency reviews on your pull requests. The action scans for vulnerable versions of dependencies introduced by package version changes in pull requests, and warns you about the associated security vulnerabilities. This gives you better visibility of what's changing in a pull request, and helps prevent vulnerabilities being added to your repository.

- [Github Guide about Dependency Review](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/supply-chain-security/understanding-your-software-supply-chain/about-dependency-review)

## Summary

This pull request is created by [StepSecurity](https://app.stepsecurity.io/securerepo) at the request of @Raj-StepSecurity. Please merge the Pull Request to incorporate the requested changes. Please tag @Raj-StepSecurity on your message if you have any questions related to the PR.
## Security Fixes

### Keeping your actions up to date with Dependabot

With Dependabot version updates, when Dependabot identifies an outdated dependency, it raises a pull request to update the manifest to the latest version of the dependency. This is recommended by GitHub as well as The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF).

- [GitHub Security Guide](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/dependabot/working-with-dependabot/keeping-your-actions-up-to-date-with-dependabot)
- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#dependency-update-tool)
### Add Dependency Review Workflow

The Dependency Review Workflow enforces dependency reviews on your pull requests. The action scans for vulnerable versions of dependencies introduced by package version changes in pull requests, and warns you about the associated security vulnerabilities. This gives you better visibility of what's changing in a pull request, and helps prevent vulnerabilities being added to your repository.

- [Github Guide about Dependency Review](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/supply-chain-security/understanding-your-software-supply-chain/about-dependency-review)
- [Github Guide for Configuring Dependency Review Action](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/supply-chain-security/understanding-your-software-supply-chain/configuring-dependency-review#using-inline-configuration-to-set-up-the-dependency-review-action)

## Summary

This pull request is created by [StepSecurity](https://app.stepsecurity.io/securerepo) at the request of @anurag-stepsecurity. Please merge the Pull Request to incorporate the requested changes. Please tag @anurag-stepsecurity on your message if you have any questions related to the PR.
## Security Fixes

### Keeping your actions up to date with Dependabot

With Dependabot version updates, when Dependabot identifies an outdated dependency, it raises a pull request to update the manifest to the latest version of the dependency. This is recommended by GitHub as well as The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF).

- [GitHub Security Guide](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/dependabot/working-with-dependabot/keeping-your-actions-up-to-date-with-dependabot)
- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#dependency-update-tool)
### Add Dependency Review Workflow

The Dependency Review Workflow enforces dependency reviews on your pull requests. The action scans for vulnerable versions of dependencies introduced by package version changes in pull requests, and warns you about the associated security vulnerabilities. This gives you better visibility of what's changing in a pull request, and helps prevent vulnerabilities being added to your repository.

- [Github Guide about Dependency Review](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/supply-chain-security/understanding-your-software-supply-chain/about-dependency-review)
- [Github Guide for Configuring Dependency Review Action](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/supply-chain-security/understanding-your-software-supply-chain/configuring-dependency-review#using-inline-configuration-to-set-up-the-dependency-review-action)
### Add OpenSSF Scorecard Workflow

OpenSSF Scorecard is an automated tool that assesses a number of important heuristics ("checks") associated with software security and assigns each check a score of 0-10. Y

### Keeping your actions up to date with Dependabot

With Dependabot version updates, when Dependabot identifies an outdated dependency, it raises a pull request to update the manifest to the latest version of the dependency. This is recommended by GitHub as well as The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF).

### Detect Vulnerabilities with SAST Workflow 

Static Code Analysis (also known as Source Code Analysis) is usually performed as part of a Code Review (also known as clear-box testing) and is carried out at the Implementation phase of a Security Development Lifecycle (SDL). Static Code Analysis commonly refers to the running of Static Code Analysis tools that attempt to highlight possible vulnerabilities within ‘static’ (non-running) source code by using techniques such as Taint Analysis and Data Flow Analysis.

- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#sast)
- [OWASP Static Code Analysis](https://owasp.org/www-community/controls/Static_Code_Analysis)
- [Github Guide For Code Scanning](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/code-scanning/automatically-scanning-your-code-for-vulnerabilities-and-errors/setting-up-code-scanning-for-a-repository)

This pull request has been generated by [StepSecurity](https://app.stepsecurity.io/github/NeckBeardPrince/actions/dashboard) as part of your enterprise subscription to ensure compliance with recommended security best practices. Please review and merge the pull request to apply these security enhancements.

## Security Fixes

### Harden Runner

Harden-Runner is an open-source security agent for the GitHub-hosted runner to prevent software supply chain attacks. It prevents exfiltration of credentials, detects tampering of source code during build, and enables running jobs without sudo access.

- [GitHub Security Guide](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions)
- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#dangerous-workflow)

### Pinned Dependencies

Pinning GitHub Actions to specific versions or commit SHAs ensures that your workflows remain consistent and secure.
Unpinned actions can lead to unexpected changes or vulnerabilities caused by upstream updates.

- [GitHub Security Guide](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions#using-third-party-actions)
- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#pinned-dependencies)
### Maintain Code Quality with Pre-Commit

Pre-commit is a framework for managing and maintaining multi-language pre-commit hooks. Hooks can be any scripts, code, or binaries that run at any stage of the git workflow. Pre-commit hooks are useful for enforcing code quality, code formatting, and detecting security vulnerabilities.

- [Official Pre-commit documentation](https://pre-commit.com/)
- [Getting Started guide](https://pre-commit.com/#getting-started)

## Security Fixes

### Least Privileged GitHub Actions Token Permissions

The GITHUB_TOKEN is an automatically generated secret to make authenticated calls to the GitHub API. GitHub recommends setting minimum token permissions for the GITHUB_TOKEN.

- [GitHub Security Guide](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-guides/automatic-token-authentication#using-the-github_token-in-a-workflow)
- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#token-permissions)
### Add Dependency Review Workflow

The Dependency Review Workflow enforces dependency reviews on your pull requests. The action scans for vulnerable versions of dependencies introduced by package version changes in pull requests, and warns you about the associated security vulnerabilities. This gives you better visibility of what's changing in a pull request, and helps prevent vulnerabilities being added to your repository.

- [Github Guide about Dependency Review](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/supply-chain-security/understanding-your-software-supply-chain/about-dependency-review)
- [Github Guide for Configuring Dependency Review Action](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/supply-chain-security/understanding-your-software-supply-chain/configuring-dependency-review#using-inline-configuration-to-set-up-the-dependency-review-action)
### Add OpenSSF Scorecard Workflow

## Summary

This pull request has been generated by [StepSecurity](https://app.stepsecurity.io/github/khenderson20/actions/dashboard) as part of your enterprise subscription to ensure compliance with recommended security best practices. Please review and merge the pull request to apply these security enhancements.

## Security Fixes

### Harden Runner

Harden-Runner is an open-source security agent for the GitHub-hosted runner to prevent software supply chain attacks. It prevents exfiltration of credentials, detects tampering of source code during build, and enables running jobs without sudo access.

- [GitHub Security Guide](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions)
- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#dangerous-workflow)

### Pinned Dependencies

Pinning GitHub Actions to specific versions or commit SHAs ensures that your workflows remain consistent and secure.
Unpinned actions can lead to unexpected changes or vulnerabilities caused by upstream updates.

- [GitHub Security Guide](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions#using-third-party-actions)
- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#pinned-dependencies)
### StepSecurity Maintained Actions

Risky GitHub Actions can expose your project to potential security risks. Risky actions have been replaced with StepSecurity maintained actions, that are secure drop-in replacements.

- [StepSecurity Maintained Actions](https://docs.stepsecurity.io/actions/stepsecurity-maintained-actions)

## Summary

This pull request is created by [StepSecurity](https://app.stepsecurity.io/securerepo) at the request of @aardbol. Please merge the Pull Request to incorporate the requested changes. Please tag @aardbol on your message if you have any questions related to the PR.
## Security Fixes

### Add Dependency Review Workflow

The Dependency Review Workflow enforces dependency reviews on your pull requests. The action scans for vulnerable versions of dependencies introduced by package version changes in pull requests, and warns you about the associated security vulnerabilities. This gives you better visibility of what's changing in a pull request, and helps prevent vulnerabilities being added to your repository.

- [Github Guide about Dependency Review](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/supply-chain-security/understanding-your-software-supply-chain/about-dependency-review)
- [Github Guide for Configuring Dependency Review Action](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/supply-chain-security/understanding-your-software-supply-chain/configuring-dependency-review#using-inline-configuration-to-set-up-the-dependency-review-action)
### Maintain Code Quality with Pre-Commit

Pre-commit is a framework for managing and maintaining multi-language pre-commit hooks. Hooks can be any scripts, code, or binaries that run at any stage of the git workflow. Pre-commit hooks are useful for enforcing code quality, code formatting, and detecting security vulnerabilities.

- [Official Pre-commit documentation](https://pre-commit.com/)
- [Getting Started guide](https://pre-commit.com/#getting-started)


## Feedback
For bug reports, feature requests, and general feedback; please email support@stepsecurity.io. To create such PRs, please visit https://app.stepsecurity.io/securerepo.


Signed-off-by: StepSecurity Bot <bot@stepsecurity.io>

## Summary

This pull request is created by [StepSecurity](https://app.stepsecurity.io/securerepo) at the request of @Moohan. Please merge the Pull Request to incorporate the requested changes. Please tag @Moohan on your message if you have any questions related to the PR.
## Security Fixes

### Pinned Dependencies

GitHub Action tags and Docker tags are mutable. This poses a security risk. GitHub's Security Hardening guide recommends pinning actions to full length commit.

- [GitHub Security Guide](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions#using-third-party-actions)
- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#pinned-dependencies)
### Add Dependency Review Workflow

The Dependency Review Workflow enforces dependency reviews on your pull requests. The action scans for vulnerable versions of dependencies introduced by package version changes in pull requests, and warns you about the associated security vulnerabilities. This gives you better visibility of what's changing in a pull request, and helps prevent vulnerabilities being added to your repository.

- [Github Guide about Dependency Review](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/supply-chain-security/understanding-your-software-supply-chain/about-dependency-review)
- [Github Guide for Configuring Dependency Review Action](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/supply-chain-security/understanding-your-software-supply-chain/configuring-dependency-review#using-inline-configuration-to-set-up-the-dependency-review-action)
### Maintain Code Quality with Pre-Commit

Pre-commit is a framework for managing and maintaining multi-language pre-commit hooks. Hooks can be any scripts, code, or binaries that run at any stage of the git workflow. Pre-commit hooks are useful for enforcing code quality, code formatting, and detecting security vulnerabilities.

- [Official Pre-commit documentation](https://pre-commit.com/)
- [Getting Started guide](https://pre-commit.com/#getting-started)

- [GitHub Security Guide](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions)

### Pinned Dependencies

Pinning GitHub Actions to specific versions or commit SHAs ensures that your workflows remain consistent and secure.
Unpinned actions can lead to unexpected changes or vulnerabilities caused by upstream updates.

## Security Fixes

With Dependabot version updates, when Dependabot identifies an outdated dependency, it raises a pull request to update the manifest to the latest version of the dependency. This is recommended by GitHub as well as The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF).

- [GitHub Security Guide](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/dependabot/working-with-dependabot/keeping-your-actions-up-to-date-with-dependabot)
- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#dependency-update-tool)
### Add Dependency Review Workflow

The Dependency Review Workflow enforces dependency reviews on your pull requests. The action scans for vulnerable versions of dependencies introduced by package version changes in pull requests, and warns you about the associated security vulnerabilities. This gives you better visibility of what's changing in a pull request, and helps prevent vulnerabilities being added to your repository.

- [Github Guide about Dependency Review](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/supply-chain-security/understanding-your-software-supply-chain/about-dependency-review)

## Summary

This pull request is created by [StepSecurity](https://app.stepsecurity.io/securerepo) at the request of @Harvester57. Please merge the Pull Request to incorporate the requested changes. Please tag @Harvester57 on your message if you have any questions related to the PR.
## Security Fixes

### Least Privileged GitHub Actions Token Permissions

The GITHUB_TOKEN is an automatically generated secret to make authenticated calls to the GitHub API. GitHub recommends setting minimum token permissions for the GITHUB_TOKEN.

- [GitHub Security Guide](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-guides/automatic-token-authentication#using-the-github_token-in-a-workflow)
- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#token-permissions)
### Pinned Dependencies

GitHub Action tags and Docker tags are mutable. This poses a security risk. GitHub's Security Hardening guide recommends pinning actions to full length commit.

- [GitHub Security Guide](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions#using-third-party-actions)
- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#pinned-dependencies)
### Maintain Code Quality with Pre-Commit

Pre-commit is a framework for managing and maintaining multi-language pre-commit hooks. Hooks can be any scripts, code, or binaries that run at any stage of the git workflow. Pre-commit hooks are useful for enforcing code quality, code formatting, and detecting security vulnerabilities.

- [Official Pre-commit documentation](https://pre-commit.com/)
- [Getting Started guide](https://pre-commit.com/#getting-started)


## Feedback
For bug reports, feature requests, and general feedback; please email support@stepsecurity.io. To create such PRs, please visit https://app.stepsecurity.io/securerepo.


Signed-off-by: StepSecurity Bot <bot@stepsecurity.io>

Static Code Analysis commonly refers to the running of Static Code Analysis tools that attempt to highlight possible vulnerabilities within ‘static’ (non-running) source code by using techniques such as Taint Analysis and Data Flow Analysis.

This pull request is created by [StepSecurity](https://app.stepsecurity.io/securerepo) at the request of @Raj-StepSecurity. Please merge the Pull Request to incorporate the requested changes. Please tag @Raj-StepSecurity on your message if you have any questions related to the PR.
## Security Fixes

### Pinned Dependencies

GitHub Action tags and Docker tags are mutable. This poses a security risk. GitHub's Security Hardening guide recommends pinning actions to full length commit.

- [GitHub Security Guide](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions#using-third-party-actions)
- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#pinned-dependencies)
### Keeping your actions up to date with Dependabot

With Dependabot version updates, when Dependabot identifies an outdated dependency, it raises a pull request to update the manifest to the latest version of the dependency. This is recommended by GitHub as well as The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF).

- [GitHub Security Guide](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/dependabot/working-with-dependabot/keeping-your-actions-up-to-date-with-dependabot)
- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#dependency-update-tool)
### Add Dependency Review Workflow

The Dependency Review Workflow enforces dependency reviews on your pull requests. The action scans for vulnerable versions of dependencies introduced by package version changes in pull requests, and warns you about the associated security vulnerabilities. This gives you better visibility of what's changing in a pull request, and helps prevent vulnerabilities being added to your repository.

- [Github Guide about Dependency Review](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/supply-chain-security/understanding-your-software-supply-chain/about-dependency-review)

## Security Fixes

### Detect Vulnerabilities with SAST Workflow 

Static Code Analysis (also known as Source Code Analysis) is usually performed as part of a Code Review (also known as clear-box testing) and is carried out at the Implementation phase of a Security Development Lifecycle (SDL). Static Code Analysis commonly refers to the running of Static Code Analysis tools that attempt to highlight possible vulnerabilities within ‘static’ (non-running) source code by using techniques such as Taint Analysis and Data Flow Analysis.

### Add Dependency Review Workflow

The Dependency Review Workflow enforces dependency reviews on your pull requests. The action scans for vulnerable versions of dependencies introduced by package version changes in pull requests, and warns you about the associated security vulnerabilities. This gives you better visibility of what's changing in a pull request, and helps prevent vulnerabilities being added to your repository.

- [Github Guide about Dependency Review](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/supply-chain-security/understanding-your-software-supply-chain/about-dependency-review)

## Summary

This pull request is created by [StepSecurity](https://app.stepsecurity.io/securerepo) at the request of @Raj-StepSecurity. Please merge the Pull Request to incorporate the requested changes. Please tag @Raj-StepSecurity on your message if you have any questions related to the PR.
## Security Fixes

### Detect Vulnerabilities with SAST Workflow 

Static Code Analysis (also known as Source Code Analysis) is usually performed as part of a Code Review (also known as clear-box testing) and is carried out at the Implementation phase of a Security Development Lifecycle (SDL). Static Code Analysis commonly refers to the running of Static Code Analysis tools that attempt to highlight possible vulnerabilities within ‘static’ (non-running) source code by using techniques such as Taint Analysis and Data Flow Analysis.

- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#sast)
- [OWASP Static Code Analysis](https://owasp.org/www-community/controls/Static_Code_Analysis)
- [Github Guide For Code Scanning](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/code-scanning/automatically-scanning-your-code-for-vulnerabilities-and-errors/setting-up-code-scanning-for-a-repository)
### Maintain Code Quality with Pre-Commit

Pre-commit is a framework for managing and maintaining multi-language pre-commit hooks. Hooks can be any scripts, code, or binaries that run at any stage of the git workflow. Pre-commit hooks are useful for enforcing code quality, code formatting, and detecting security vulnerabilities.

- [Official Pre-commit documentation](https://pre-commit.com/)
- [Getting Started guide](https://pre-commit.com/#getting-started)


## Feedback
For bug reports, feature requests, and general feedback; please email support@stepsecurity.io. To create such PRs, please visit https://app.stepsecurity.io/securerepo.

## Summary

This pull request has been generated by [StepSecurity](https://app.stepsecurity.io/github/step-security/actions/dashboard) as part of your enterprise subscription to ensure compliance with recommended security best practices. Please review and merge the pull request to apply these security enhancements.

## Security Fixes

### Harden Runner

Harden-Runner is an open-source security agent for the GitHub-hosted runner to prevent software supply chain attacks. It prevents exfiltration of credentials, detects tampering of source code during build, and enables running jobs without sudo access.

- [GitHub Security Guide](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions)
- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#dangerous-workflow)

### Pinned Dependencies

Pinning GitHub Actions to specific versions or commit SHAs ensures that your workflows remain consistent and secure.
Unpinned actions can lead to unexpected changes or vulnerabilities caused by upstream updates.

- [GitHub Security Guide](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions#using-third-party-actions)
- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#pinned-dependencies)

## Security Fixes

### Pinned Dependencies

GitHub Action tags and Docker tags are mutable. This poses a security risk. GitHub's Security Hardening guide recommends pinning actions to full length commit.

- [GitHub Security Guide](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions#using-third-party-actions)
- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#pinned-dependencies)
### Maintain Code Quality with Pre-Commit

Pre-commit is a framework for managing and maintaining multi-language pre-commit hooks. Hooks can be any scripts, code, or binaries that run at any stage of the git workflow. Pre-commit hooks are useful for enforcing code quality, code formatting, and detecting security vulnerabilities.

- [Official Pre-commit documentation](https://pre-commit.com/)
- [Getting Started guide](https://pre-commit.com/#getting-started)

Static Code Analysis commonly refers to the running of Static Code Analysis tools that attempt to highlight possible vulnerabilities within ‘static’ (non-running) source code by using techniques such as Taint Analysis and Data Flow Analysis.

- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#sast)
- [OWASP Static Code Analysis](https://owasp.org/www-community/controls/Static_Code_Analysis)

GitHub Action tags and Docker tags are mutable. This poses a security risk. GitHub's Security Hardening guide recommends pinning actions to full length commit.

- [GitHub Security Guide](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions#using-third-party-actions)
- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#pinned-dependencies)
### Keeping your actions up to date with Dependabot

With Dependabot version updates, when Dependabot identifies an outdated dependency, it raises a pull request to update the manifest to the latest version of the dependency. This is recommended by GitHub as well as The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF).

- [GitHub Security Guide](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/dependabot/working-with-dependabot/keeping-your-actions-up-to-date-with-dependabot)
- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#dependency-update-tool)

## Summary

This pull request is created by [StepSecurity](https://app.stepsecurity.io/securerepo) at the request of @Raj-StepSecurity. Please merge the Pull Request to incorporate the requested changes. Please tag @Raj-StepSecurity on your message if you have any questions related to the PR.
## Security Fixes

### Pinned Dependencies

GitHub Action tags and Docker tags are mutable. This poses a security risk. GitHub's Security Hardening guide recommends pinning actions to full length commit.

- [GitHub Security Guide](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions#using-third-party-actions)
- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#pinned-dependencies)
### Keeping your actions up to date with Dependabot

With Dependabot version updates, when Dependabot identifies an outdated dependency, it raises a pull request to update the manifest to the latest version of the dependency. This is recommended by GitHub as well as The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF).

- [GitHub Security Guide](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/dependabot/working-with-dependabot/keeping-your-actions-up-to-date-with-dependabot)
- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#dependency-update-tool)
### Secure Dockerfiles

Pin image tags to digests in Dockerfiles. With the Docker v2 API release, it became possible to use digests in place of tags when pulling images or to use them in FROM lines in Dockerfiles.

- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#pinned-dependencies)

Pinning GitHub Actions to specific versions or commit SHAs ensures that your workflows remain consistent and secure.
Unpinned actions can lead to unexpected changes or vulnerabilities caused by upstream updates.

## Summary

This pull request is created by [StepSecurity](https://app.stepsecurity.io/securerepo) at the request of @GCHQDeveloper581. Please merge the Pull Request to incorporate the requested changes. Please tag @GCHQDeveloper581 on your message if you have any questions related to the PR.
## Security Fixes

### Pinned Dependencies

GitHub Action tags and Docker tags are mutable. This poses a security risk. GitHub's Security Hardening guide recommends pinning actions to full length commit.

- [GitHub Security Guide](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions#using-third-party-actions)
- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#pinned-dependencies)
### Keeping your actions up to date with Dependabot

With Dependabot version updates, when Dependabot identifies an outdated dependency, it raises a pull request to update the manifest to the latest version of the dependency. This is recommended by GitHub as well as The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF).

- [GitHub Security Guide](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/dependabot/working-with-dependabot/keeping-your-actions-up-to-date-with-dependabot)
- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#dependency-update-tool)
### Secure Dockerfiles

Pin image tags to digests in Dockerfiles. With the Docker v2 API release, it became possible to use digests in place of tags when pulling images or to use them in FROM lines in Dockerfiles.

- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#pinned-dependencies)


## Feedback
For bug reports, feature requests, and general feedback; please email support@stepsecurity.io. To create such PRs, please visit https://app.stepsecurity.io/securerepo.


Signed-off-by: StepSecurity Bot <bot@stepsecurity.io>

The Dependency Review Workflow enforces dependency reviews on your pull requests. The action scans for vulnerable versions of dependencies introduced by package version changes in pull requests, and warns you about the associated security vulnerabilities. This gives you better visibility of what's changing in a pull request, and helps prevent vulnerabilities being added to your repository.

Pre-commit is a framework for managing and maintaining multi-language pre-commit hooks. Hooks can be any scripts, code, or binaries that run at any stage of the git workflow. Pre-commit hooks are useful for enforcing code quality, code formatting, and detecting security vulnerabilities.

With Dependabot version updates, when Dependabot identifies an outdated dependency, it raises a pull request to update the manifest to the latest version of the dependency. This is recommended by GitHub as well as The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF).

### Detect Vulnerabilities with SAST Workflow 

Static Code Analysis (also known as Source Code Analysis) is usually performed as part of a Code Review (also known as clear-box testing) and is carried out at the Implementation phase of a Security Development Lifecycle (SDL). Static Code Analysis commonly refers to the running of Static Code Analysis tools that attempt to highlight possible vulnerabilities within ‘static’ (non-running) source code by using techniques such as Taint Analysis and Data Flow Analysis.

Static Code Analysis commonly refers to the running of Static Code Analysis tools that attempt to highlight possible vulnerabilities within ‘static’ (non-running) source code by using techniques such as Taint Analysis and Data Flow Analysis.

## Security Fixes

### Detect Vulnerabilities with SAST Workflow 

Static Code Analysis (also known as Source Code Analysis) is usually performed as part of a Code Review (also known as clear-box testing) and is carried out at the Implementation phase of a Security Development Lifecycle (SDL). Static Code Analysis commonly refers to the running of Static Code Analysis tools that attempt to highlight possible vulnerabilities within ‘static’ (non-running) source code by using techniques such as Taint Analysis and Data Flow Analysis.

- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#sast)
- [OWASP Static Code Analysis](https://owasp.org/www-community/controls/Static_Code_Analysis)
- [Github Guide For Code Scanning](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/code-scanning/automatically-scanning-your-code-for-vulnerabilities-and-errors/setting-up-code-scanning-for-a-repository)
### Add Dependency Review Workflow

The Dependency Review Workflow enforces dependency reviews on your pull requests. The action scans for vulnerable versions of dependencies introduced by package version changes in pull requests, and warns you about the associated security vulnerabilities. This gives you better visibility of what's changing in a pull request, and helps prevent vulnerabilities being added to your repository.

- [Github Guide about Dependency Review](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/supply-chain-security/understanding-your-software-supply-chain/about-dependency-review)
- [Github Guide for Configuring Dependency Review Action](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/supply-chain-security/understanding-your-software-supply-cha

This pull request is created by [StepSecurity](https://app.stepsecurity.io/securerepo) at the request of @kgiusti. Please merge the Pull Request to incorporate the requested changes. Please tag @kgiusti on your message if you have any questions related to the PR.
## Security Fixes

### Pinned Dependencies

GitHub Action tags and Docker tags are mutable. This poses a security risk. GitHub's Security Hardening guide recommends pinning actions to full length commit.

- [GitHub Security Guide](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions#using-third-party-actions)
- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#pinned-dependencies)
### Secure Dockerfiles

Pin image tags to digests in Dockerfiles. With the Docker v2 API release, it became possible to use digests in place of tags when pulling images or to use them in FROM lines in Dockerfiles.

- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#pinned-dependencies)


## Feedback
For bug reports, feature requests, and general feedback; please email support@stepsecurity.io. To create such PRs, please visit https://app.stepsecurity.io/securerepo.

## Summary

This pull request is created by [StepSecurity](https://app.stepsecurity.io/securerepo) at the request of @kgiusti. Please merge the Pull Request to incorporate the requested changes. Please tag @kgiusti on your message if you have any questions related to the PR.
## Security Fixes

### Keeping your actions up to date with Dependabot

With Dependabot version updates, when Dependabot identifies an outdated dependency, it raises a pull request to update the manifest to the latest version of the dependency. This is recommended by GitHub as well as The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF).

- [GitHub Security Guide](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/dependabot/working-with-dependabot/keeping-your-actions-up-to-date-with-dependabot)
- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#dependency-update-tool)
### Add Dependency Review Workflow

The Dependency Review Workflow enforces dependency reviews on your pull requests. The action scans for vulnerable versions of dependencies introduced by package version changes in pull requests, and warns you about the associated security vulnerabilities. This gives you better visibility of what's changing in a pull request, and helps prevent vulnerabilities being added to your repository.

- [Github Guide about Dependency Review](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/supply-chain-security/understanding-your-software-supply-chain/about-dependency-review)
- [Github Guide for Configuring Dependency Review Action](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/supply-chain-security/understanding-your-software-supply-chain/configuring-dependency-review#using-inline-configuration-to-set-up-the-dependency-review-action)


## Feedback

## Summary

This pull request has been generated by [StepSecurity](https://app.stepsecurity.io/github/step-security/actions/dashboard) as part of your enterprise subscription to ensure compliance with recommended security best practices. Please review and merge the pull request to apply these security enhancements.

## Security Fixes

### Harden Runner

Harden-Runner is an open-source security agent for the GitHub-hosted runner to prevent software supply chain attacks. It prevents exfiltration of credentials, detects tampering of source code during build, and enables running jobs without sudo access.

- [GitHub Security Guide](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions)
- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#dangerous-workflow)

### Pinned Dependencies

Pinning GitHub Actions to specific versions or commit SHAs ensures that your workflows remain consistent and secure.
Unpinned actions can lead to unexpected changes or vulnerabilities caused by upstream updates.

- [GitHub Security Guide](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions#using-third-party-actions)
- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#pinned-dependencies)

oakoss/linesmith.author: step-security-bot
oakoss/linesmith.body:
Cherry-picked from the StepSecurity remediation PR. Adds the harden-runner step to the release-plz workflow as the first job step, in `egress-policy: audit` mode — consistent with the pattern landed across ci/audit/codeql via lsm-vj7.

The other StepSecurity proposals were deferred or rejected on this branch:
- `dependabot.yml` — conflicts with planned Renovate (lsm-yu0).
- `dependency-review.yml` — overlaps with cargo-deny in audit.yml.
- `scorecards.yml` — most checks already pass; defer until lsm-j2o lands branch protection.
- `pre-commit-config.yaml` — conflicts with our existing lefthook setup.

With Dependabot version updates, when Dependabot identifies an outdated dependency, it raises a pull request to update the manifest to the latest version of the dependency. This is recommended by GitHub as well as The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF).

### Add Dependency Review Workflow

The Dependency Review Workflow enforces dependency reviews on your pull requests. The action scans for vulnerable versions of dependencies introduced by package version changes in pull requests, and warns you about the associated security vulnerabilities. This gives you better visibility of what's changing in a pull request, and helps prevent vulnerabilities being added to your repository.

- [Github Guide about Dependency Review](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/supply-chain-security/understanding-your-software-supply-chain/about-dependency-review)
- [Github Guide for Configuring Dependency Review Action](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/supply-chain-security/understanding-your-software-supply-chain/configuring-dependency-review#using-inline-configuration-to-set-up-the-dependency-review-action)

A *pinned dependency* is a dependency that is explicitly set to a specific hashed version instead of a mutable version. Pinned dependencis ensure that development and deployment are done with the same software versions which reduces deployment risks, and enables reproducibility. It can help mitigate compromised dependencies from undermining the security of the project in certain scenarios. The dependencies were pinned using [Secure WorkFlows](https://github.com/step-security/secure-workflows)

## Security Fixes

### Pinned Dependencies

GitHub Action tags and Docker tags are mutable. This poses a security risk. GitHub's Security Hardening guide recommends pinning actions to full length commit.

- [GitHub Security Guide](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions#using-third-party-actions)
- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#pinned-dependencies)
### Keeping your actions up to date with Dependabot

With Dependabot version updates, when Dependabot identifies an outdated dependency, it raises a pull request to update the manifest to the latest version of the dependency. This is recommended by GitHub as well as The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF).

- [GitHub Security Guide](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/dependabot/working-with-dependabot/keeping-your-actions-up-to-date-with-dependabot)
- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#dependency-update-tool)
### Secure Dockerfiles

Pin image tags to digests in Dockerfiles. With the Docker v2 API release, it became possible to use digests in place of tags when pulling images or to use them in FROM lines in Dockerfiles.

- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#pinned-dependencies)

## Security Fixes

### Least Privileged GitHub Actions Token Permissions

The GITHUB_TOKEN is an automatically generated secret to make authenticated calls to the GitHub API. GitHub recommends setting minimum token permissions for the GITHUB_TOKEN.

- [GitHub Security Guide](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-guides/automatic-token-authentication#using-the-github_token-in-a-workflow)
- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#token-permissions)
### Add Dependency Review Workflow

The Dependency Review Workflow enforces dependency reviews on your pull requests. The action scans for vulnerable versions of dependencies introduced by package version changes in pull requests, and warns you about the associated security vulnerabilities. This gives you better visibility of what's changing in a pull request, and helps prevent vulnerabilities being added to your repository.

- [Github Guide about Dependency Review](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/supply-chain-security/understanding-your-software-supply-chain/about-dependency-review)
- [Github Guide for Configuring Dependency Review Action](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/supply-chain-security/understanding-your-software-supply-chain/configuring-dependency-review#using-inline-configuration-to-set-up-the-dependency-review-action)

## Summary

This pull request is created by [StepSecurity](https://app.stepsecurity.io/securerepo) at the request of @rajbos. Please merge the Pull Request to incorporate the requested changes. Please tag @rajbos on your message if you have any questions related to the PR.
## Security Fixes

### Detect Vulnerabilities with SAST Workflow 

Static Code Analysis (also known as Source Code Analysis) is usually performed as part of a Code Review (also known as clear-box testing) and is carried out at the Implementation phase of a Security Development Lifecycle (SDL). Static Code Analysis commonly refers to the running of Static Code Analysis tools that attempt to highlight possible vulnerabilities within ‘static’ (non-running) source code by using techniques such as Taint Analysis and Data Flow Analysis.

- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#sast)
- [OWASP Static Code Analysis](https://owasp.org/www-community/controls/Static_Code_Analysis)
- [Github Guide For Code Scanning](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/code-scanning/automatically-scanning-your-code-for-vulnerabilities-and-errors/setting-up-code-scanning-for-a-repository)
### Add OpenSSF Scorecard Workflow

OpenSSF Scorecard is an automated tool that assesses a number of important heuristics ("checks") associated with software security and assigns each check a score of 0-10. You can use these scores to understand specific areas to improve in order to strengthen the security posture of your project.

Scorecard workflow also allows maintainers to display a Scorecard badge on their repository to show off their hard work.

- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Scorecard](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard)

## Security Fixes

### Keeping your actions up to date with Dependabot

With Dependabot version updates, when Dependabot identifies an outdated dependency, it raises a pull request to update the manifest to the latest version of the dependency. This is recommended by GitHub as well as The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF).

- [GitHub Security Guide](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/dependabot/working-with-dependabot/keeping-your-actions-up-to-date-with-dependabot)

Static Code Analysis (also known as Source Code Analysis) is usually performed as part of a Code Review (also known as clear-box testing) and is carried out at the Implementation phase of a Security Development Lifecycle (SDL). Static Code Analysis commonly refers to the running of Static Code Analysis tools that attempt to highlight possible vulnerabilities within ‘static’ (non-running) source code by using techniques such as Taint Analysis and Data Flow Analysis.

## Summary

This pull request is created by [Secure Workflows](https://app.stepsecurity.io/securerepo) at the request of @rajbos. Please merge the Pull Request to incorporate the requested changes. Please tag @rajbos on your message if you have any questions related to the PR. You can also engage with the [StepSecurity](https://github.com/step-security) team by tagging @step-security-bot.

## Security Fixes

### Pinned Dependencies

A *pinned dependency* is a dependency that is explicitly set to a specific hashed version instead of a mutable version. Pinned dependencis ensure that development and deployment are done with the same software versions which reduces deployment risks, and enables reproducibility. It can help mitigate compromised dependencies from undermining the security of the project in certain scenarios. The dependencies were pinned using [Secure WorkFlows](https://github.com/step-security/secure-workflows)

- [GitHub Security Guide](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions#using-third-party-actions)
- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#pinned-dependencies)


## Feedback
For bug reports, feature requests, and general feedback; please create an issue in [step-security/secure-workflows](https://github.com/step-security/secure-workflows). To create such PRs, please visit https://app.stepsecurity.io/securerepo.

This pull request is created by [StepSecurity](https://app.stepsecurity.io/securerepo) at the request of @3rr0r-505. Please merge the Pull Request to incorporate the requested changes. Please tag @3rr0r-505 on your message if you have any questions related to the PR.
## Security Fixes

### Detect Vulnerabilities with SAST Workflow 

Static Code Analysis (also known as Source Code Analysis) is usually performed as part of a Code Review (also known as clear-box testing) and is carried out at the Implementation phase of a Security Development Lifecycle (SDL). Static Code Analysis commonly refers to the running of Static Code Analysis tools that attempt to highlight possible vulnerabilities within ‘static’ (non-running) source code by using techniques such as Taint Analysis and Data Flow Analysis.

- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#sast)
- [OWASP Static Code Analysis](https://owasp.org/www-community/controls/Static_Code_Analysis)

### Add Dependency Review Workflow

The Dependency Review Workflow enforces dependency reviews on your pull requests. The action scans for vulnerable versions of dependencies introduced by package version changes in pull requests, and warns you about the associated security vulnerabilities. This gives you better visibility of what's changing in a pull request, and helps prevent vulnerabilities being added to your repository.

- [Github Guide about Dependency Review](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/supply-chain-security/understanding-your-software-supply-chain/about-dependency-review)
- [Github Guide for Configuring Dependency Review Action](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/supply-chain-security/understanding-your-software-supply-chain

## Summary

This pull request is created by [StepSecurity](https://app.stepsecurity.io/securerepo) at the request of @texarr. Please merge the Pull Request to incorporate the requested changes. Please tag @texarr on your message if you have any questions related to the PR.
## Security Fixes

### Add Dependency Review Workflow

The Dependency Review Workflow enforces dependency reviews on your pull requests. The action scans for vulnerable versions of dependencies introduced by package version changes in pull requests, and warns you about the associated security vulnerabilities. This gives you better visibility of what's changing in a pull request, and helps prevent vulnerabilities being added to your repository.

- [Github Guide about Dependency Review](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/supply-chain-security/understanding-your-software-supply-chain/about-dependency-review)
- [Github Guide for Configuring Dependency Review Action](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/supply-chain-security/understanding-your-software-supply-chain/configuring-dependency-review#using-inline-configuration-to-set-up-the-dependency-review-action)
### Add OpenSSF Scorecard Workflow

OpenSSF Scorecard is an automated tool that assesses a number of important heuristics ("checks") associated with software security and assigns each check a score of 0-10. You can use these scores to understand specific areas to improve in order to strengthen the security posture of your project.

Scorecard workflow also allows maintainers to display a Scorecard badge on their repository to show off their hard work.

- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Scorecard](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard)
### Maintain Code Quality with Pre-Commit

A *pinned dependency* is a dependency that is explicitly set to a specific hashed version instead of a mutable version. Pinned dependencis ensure that development and deployment are done with the same software versions which reduces deployment risks, and enables reproducibility. It can help mitigate compromised dependencies from undermining the security of the project in certain scenarios. The dependencies were pinned using [Secure WorkFlows](https://github.com/step-security/secure-workflows)

The package ecosystem to update github-actions is added using [Secure WorkFlows](https://github.com/step-security/secure-workflows). This is recommended by GitHub as well as The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF).

This pull request is created by [StepSecurity](https://app.stepsecurity.io/securerepo) at the request of @cpuguy83. Please merge the Pull Request to incorporate the requested changes. Please tag @cpuguy83 on your message if you have any questions related to the PR.
## Security Fixes

### Keeping your actions up to date with Dependabot

With Dependabot version updates, when Dependabot identifies an outdated dependency, it raises a pull request to update the manifest to the latest version of the dependency. This is recommended by GitHub as well as The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF).

- [GitHub Security Guide](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/dependabot/working-with-dependabot/keeping-your-actions-up-to-date-with-dependabot)
- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#dependency-update-tool)
### Secure Dockerfiles

Pin image tags to digests in Dockerfiles. With the Docker v2 API release, it became possible to use digests in place of tags when pulling images or to use them in FROM lines in Dockerfiles.

- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#pinned-dependencies)


## Feedback
For bug reports, feature requests, and general feedback; please email support@stepsecurity.io. To create such PRs, please visit https://app.stepsecurity.io/securerepo.

gander-tools/osm-tagging-schema-mcp.title: [StepSecurity] Apply security best practices
gander-tools/osm-tagging-schema-mcp.author: step-security-bot
gander-tools/osm-tagging-schema-mcp.body:
<!-- kody-pr-summary:start -->
This pull request strengthens the repository’s security posture by adding automated scanning and tighter CI/CD safeguards.

### Key changes
- **Automated dependency updates (Dependabot):** Adds a `dependabot.yml` configuration to check for updates **daily** across:
  - GitHub Actions workflows
  - Docker dependencies (both repository root and `/.ossfuzz`)
  - npm dependencies

- **Hardened GitHub Actions runners:** Updates multiple existing workflows to run `step-security/harden-runner` with **egress traffic auditing**, increasing visibility into outbound network calls made during CI jobs.

- **CodeQL security analysis:** Introduces a new **CodeQL** workflow that runs on:
  - Pushes to `master`
  - Pull requests targeting `master`
  - A weekly schedule  
  It analyzes **JavaScript and TypeScript** and uploads results to GitHub Security.

- **Workflow permission tightening:** Adds explicit default workflow permissions (`contents: read`) to the Docker publishing workflow to reduce the default token scope.

- **Pre-commit security and hygiene hooks:** Adds a `.pre-commit-config.yaml` enabling local checks for:
  - Secret detection (`gitleaks`)
  - Shell script linting (`shellcheck`)
  - JavaScript linting (`eslint`)
  - Basic formatting fixes (trailing whitespace, end-of-file)
<!-- kody-pr-summary:end -->

This PR applies security best practices across the repository by adding automated dependency and code security checks and strengthening CI execution:

- **Enable automated dependency updates (Dependabot):** Adds a `.github/dependabot.yml` configuration to check **daily** for updates across:
  - GitHub Actions workflows
  - Docker dependencies in both `/.ossfuzz` and the repository root
  - npm dependencies in the repository root

- **Add CodeQL static analysis:** Introduces a new `CodeQL` GitHub Actions workflow to run security/code scanning for **JavaScript and TypeScript** on:
  - pushes to `master`
  - pull requests targeting `master`
  - a weekly scheduled run

- **Harden GitHub Actions runners:** Updates existing workflows to run `step-security/harden-runner` with an **egress policy set to `audit`**, providing visibility into outbound network calls during CI jobs.

- **Add pre-commit security/quality hooks:** Introduces a `.pre-commit-config.yaml` to run local checks including:
  - secret scanning via **gitleaks**
  - **shellcheck**
  - **eslint**
  - whitespace/end-of-file formatting fixes
<!-- kody-pr-summary:end -->

gander-tools/osm-tagging-schema-mcp.title: [StepSecurity] ci: Harden GitHub Actions
gander-tools/osm-tagging-schema-mcp.author: step-security-bot
gander-tools/osm-tagging-schema-mcp.body:
<!-- kody-pr-summary:start -->
This pull request hardens the repository’s GitHub Actions CI workflows by adding the **StepSecurity hardened runner** step to audit outbound network traffic during job execution.

### What changed
Across multiple workflows, a new first step is added to relevant jobs:

- **Uses:** `step-security/harden-runner@v2.16.0` (pinned to a specific commit)
- **Mode:** `egress-policy: audit` (logs/audits outbound calls rather than blocking them)

### Workflows updated
- `actionlint.yml`
- `auto-cleanup.yml`
- `auto-pr.yml`
- `dependency-review.yml`
- `fuzz.yml`
- `labeler.yml`
- `publish-docker.yml`
- `renovate-config-validation.yml`
- `security-main.yml`
- `security-pr.yml`
- `test.yml`

### Functional impact
CI jobs now **record/audit outbound network connections** made during workflow runs, improving visibility into external communications for security monitoring and review, without changing job behavior by enforcing blocks.
<!-- kody-pr-summary:end -->

## Security Fixes

### Add OpenSSF Scorecard Workflow

OpenSSF Scorecard is an automated tool that assesses a number of important heuristics ("checks") associated with software security and assigns each check a score of 0-10. You can use these scores to understand specific areas to improve in order to strengthen the security posture of your project.

Scorecard workflow also allows maintainers to display a Scorecard badge on their repository to show off their hard work.

- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Scorecard](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard)

## Summary

This pull request is created by [StepSecurity](https://app.stepsecurity.io/securerepo) at the request of @yelinaung. Please merge the Pull Request to incorporate the requested changes. Please tag @yelinaung on your message if you have any questions related to the PR.
## Security Fixes

### Least Privileged GitHub Actions Token Permissions

The GITHUB_TOKEN is an automatically generated secret to make authenticated calls to the GitHub API. GitHub recommends setting minimum token permissions for the GITHUB_TOKEN.

- [GitHub Security Guide](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-guides/automatic-token-authentication#using-the-github_token-in-a-workflow)
- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#token-permissions)
### Keeping your actions up to date with Dependabot

With Dependabot version updates, when Dependabot identifies an outdated dependency, it raises a pull request to update the manifest to the latest version of the dependency. This is recommended by GitHub as well as The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF).

- [GitHub Security Guide](https://docs.github.com/en/code-security/dependabot/working-with-dependabot/keeping-your-actions-up-to-date-with-dependabot)
- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#dependency-update-tool)
### Maintain Code Quality with Pre-Commit

Pre-commit is a framework for managing and maintaining multi-language pre-commit hooks. Hooks can be any scripts, code, or binaries that run at any stage of the git workflow. Pre-commit hooks are useful for enforcing code quality, code formatting, and detecting security vulnerabilities.

- [Official Pre-commit documentation](https://pre-commit.com/)
- [Getting Started guide](https://pre-commit.com/#getting-started)


## Feedback
For bug reports, feature requests, and general feedback; please email support@stepsecurity.

## Summary

This pull request has been generated by [StepSecurity](https://app.stepsecurity.io/github/jeasmith/actions/dashboard) as part of your enterprise subscription to ensure compliance with recommended security best practices. Please review and merge the pull request to apply these security enhancements.

## Security Fixes

### Harden Runner

Harden-Runner is an open-source security agent for the GitHub-hosted runner to prevent software supply chain attacks. It prevents exfiltration of credentials, detects tampering of source code during build, and enables running jobs without sudo access.

- [GitHub Security Guide](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/security-for-github-actions/security-guides/security-hardening-for-github-actions)
- [The Open Source Security Foundation (OpenSSF) Security Guide](https://github.com/ossf/scorecard/blob/main/docs/checks.md#dangerous-workflow)
